messages.subject: [RQt-devel] qtinterfaces doc, tutorials, or apps built upon?
messages.subject_clean: [RQt-devel] qtinterfaces doc, tutorials, or apps built upon?
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
 could you please point me out some study material, from which to
learn how to use qtinterfaces?
I've already studied qt* vignettes, demos, and also cranvas sources,
but still - the limited qt* doc makes developing quite slow.
Are there any other resources, please?
Or maybe some apps built upon qt*, possibly some that combine qtpaint
painting with qtbase GUI?

regards,
 Tomas

messages.subject_clean: [RQt-devel] qtinterfaces doc, tutorials, or apps built upon?
messages.body_plain:
There are not too many applications of qtpaint right now. cranvas would
probably be the best resource. You might also check out "visnab" on github.
As far as qtbase is concerned, it is best to read the Qt documentation.
Also, John Verzani and I have written a book that will be released in the
next couple of months, I think, called "Programming GUIs in R". It explains
most of Qt from the R/qtbase perspective in about 120 pages. qtpaint is
unfortunately not described beyond the vignette.

Michael

messages.subject: [RQt-devel] qtbase built for 64 bit
messages.body_plain:
Hey guys,

I finally managed to get qtbase building for 64 bit Windows. This means we
can distribute Windows binaries through CRAN. Still need to clean up the
process for the benefit of the CRAN maintainers. And then move on to
qtpaint.

Michael
